groups.brief:
Two changes to tests/structure.py, landing together because they are the two halves of making the budget table trustworthy before #350 makes re-recording mandatory.

#370 -- record_budgets() refuses by default. Today --record rewrites every row from the current tree, so it cannot distinguish locking in a gain from laundering a regression, and the tool cannot tell the row you meant to change from the row that came along (that happened twice on 2026-09-03, both caught by a human noticing). Refuse a re-record that moves any metric the wrong way unless --allow-regression="<reason>" is passed, and write that reason into the COMMIT rather than the PR body. THE DIRECTION IS UNIFORMLY new > old FOR ALL 22 METRICS -- do not build a per-metric direction table, that is one more hand-maintained list to rot. THE CHECK MUST SKIP FRACTION_METRICS (single member: cross_seam_fraction). This REVERSES the issue body, and the argument is structural: a tolerance metric passes inside its band, so there is nothing to record, and fails outside it, so it is a decision -- there is no third case, and re-recording one can only ever loosen the band. Print old and new side by side with the direction named. Keep #363's resolvable merge-base recorded_at on the path that proceeds.

#369 -- duplication_blocks has never been able to fire: the longest duplicated run in the tree is 19 lines against a 30-line window, so the metric has been reporting 0 since the day it was recorded. DUP_BLOCK_LINES 30 -> 10 (tests/structure.py:126) and re-record duplication_blocks 0 -> the measured value, quoting the rows in the commit. Two things the fixer must SHOW rather than assert: that the count is still 0 at window 20 (which is what proves it had never been able to fire), and a duplication you construct that the new window catches. Re-measure the row line numbers on the fork rather than trusting the issue -- thermal_model's rows moved about +17 lines since it was filed, and the count is a measurement, not a target.

Both touch tests/structure_budgets.json, so they are one PR. cross_seam_fraction is never re-recorded.

groups.brief:
The other half of the ratchet, on top of W1-G1's guarded --record.

Two things decide whether this is a good gate or a hated one: the failure must print the exact runnable command (python3 tests/structure.py --record) and it must be framed as 'you made this better, write it down' -- a gate that scolds a pull request for improving the tree will be worked around, and then it protects nothing. #370's fourth comment adds a requirement the body does not have: an explicit category for metrics that are DELIBERATELY never re-recorded, or the two correct decisions already taken on cross_seam_fraction become gate violations the moment re-recording is mandatory. Acceptance, all four executed: replay #338 (five metrics improved, all named); replay a zero-headroom commit (silent); a worsening still fails; --record writes a recorded_at that is an ancestor of origin/main.

Both tables are ALREADY built and sorted in measure() (monsters, cc_scores), so this is two lines plus their budget entries. Plain counts, so the existing current > budget arm handles them: no tolerance, no new polarity, no interaction with the FRACTION_METRICS exemption. REJECT sum_cc AND PUT THE REASON IN THE DOCSTRING, not only in the issue -- it is the obvious next proposal and it is wrong, because splitting a CC-87 method into a parent and four helpers lands near 100, so a sum_cc budget would fail the exact refactor #224 exists to perform. The acceptance test that matters is the replay: run 4a7bdb6^ -> 4a7bdb6 (a legitimate extraction) and show both maxima UNCHANGED.

Adding the two keys forces a re-record in the same commit (the two-way key-set check), which is why this rides behind #370's guard rather than in front of it.

groups.brief:
One question in two issues: which files are genuinely inert, and does anything check that answer.

#372 -- stamp.py's --self-test is invoked by nothing and is in no closure, so the release gate's own test has never run. USE THE THIRD OPTION FROM THE ISSUE'S COMMENT, NOT EITHER OPTION IN THE BODY: narrow tests/closure.py's INERT entry from 'tools/' to 'tools/audit/', and wire --self-test into a lane. tools/ is on INERT because it holds write-once round-2 audit evidence -- that is tools/audit/ specifically; stamp.py was exempt only by sharing a prefix. Narrowing moves exactly one file into the must-classify set (git ls-files tools/ | grep -v '^tools/audit/' returns tools/release/stamp.py alone), the recorder then pulls the test into scope on its own, and a future change to stamp.py selects its test automatically -- no exemption, no hidden call site. Re-derive the affected closure with ./tests/derive_closures.sh under the gate lock -- a FULL derive, not --single: this diff changes closure.py itself, so the gate reports MODE: FULL and the single-script path cannot produce a table the gate will accept. The blocked review on #372 (comment 5537527625) says so with the traces, and its four red checks all reduce to the un-re-derived table. Never hand-edit closures.json. Then break one pure piece of stamp.py and show the suite goes red; a test wired in but not selected is the same defect one level up.

#357 -- quality_scale.yaml is on INERT and inside two recorded closures (env_drift.py and golden.py) at the same time. closure.py merge would fail on it today, and --record-only is what hides that: derive_closures.sh and both CI paths pass it, so the contradiction check never runs. DECIDE BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY READING: change the file, capture env_drift and golden output both ways, and see whether anything moves. If it genuinely affects output it belongs off INERT; if not, the recorded closures over-approximate, which is documented and accepted (#251/D3-09 was closed wontfix on exactly that ground) and the RECORDER is what needs looking at. Either way, add the assertion that no file is both INERT and in any recorded closure, on the path CI actually runs, and SHOW IT FAILING ON TODAY'S TREE FIRST -- the general form of this issue is that a check whose failure is visible and one whose failure is blocking look identical in a passing run.

Both edit the INERT tuple, so they are one PR: #357's new assertion is exactly the check that must not break when #372 narrows the prefix.

groups.brief:
A 'Tidy up' button on the setup page's layout editor -- a RECOVERY affordance, not a layout optimiser. Dragged card positions are persisted with no way back: LayoutEditor's own Undo only restores the snapshot taken when the editor opened, so a drag made after that snapshot has no undo path at all. About 335 production lines, all in www/heatpump-optimizer-card.js; zero Python.

THE TOPOLOGY IS SMALL AND THE ALGORITHM IS EXHAUSTIVE, NOT A HEURISTIC. At most 8 boxes and 7 pipes; with the column abscissae fixed, the search space is the product of each column's internal permutations -- 3! * 3! * 2! = 72 candidates -- so enumerate all 72 and keep the best. Exhaustive enumeration is chosen FOR DETERMINISM: a seeded annealer would make the pinned card_drift markup a function of its own cooling schedule, and a later, unrelated tuning pass could then move a golden fixture with no failing test to explain why.

Positions are already persisted through LayoutEditor.save() -> apply_topology -> CONF_TOPOLOGY_POSITIONS, so the button writes ed.positions exactly as a drag already does -- no service, no options-flow change, no store schema change.

STATE THE CROSSING BENEFIT PLAINLY: IT IS NEAR ZERO. The default column layout already yields 1-2 edge crossings and zero pipes routed over a tank on every shipped topology, and exhaustive search over all 72 candidates reaches 0/0/1/0 crossings across the topologies measured. The PR must not sell this as an optimiser -- it exists so a user who has dragged boxes into a mess has a button back to a good default, not because the default is bad.

FIXTURE COST. Exactly one card_drift state moves: layout_editing_dragged, the only state whose topology publishes a catalog and therefore the only one that renders the layout bar the button lives in. One more state moves only if the fixer adds a new state that presses the button; that additional cost stays this low only if nothing is added to cardStyleBlock() (the button reuses existing chrome).

THREE PREMISES, REFUTED, DO NOT RE-DERIVE. (1) tests/structure.py does not measure this file: it is Python-only, and the closure that reaches it skips the card. (2) .wi-viewreset is the what-if chart's reset control, unrelated to this diagram.
